claim_checks.claim: It removed the `initialize` handshake and protocol-level sessions ✅[3]
claim_checks.page_says: Remove protocol-level sessions and the Mcp-Session-Id header from the Streamable HTTP transport. … Make MCP stateless: remove the initialize/notifications/initialized handshake.
claim_checks.note: Both removals are listed as major changes in the 2026-07-28 changelog.

claim_checks.claim: A request missing a required key is rejected with `-32602`, and with HTTP 400 on HTTP ✅[7]
claim_checks.page_says: A request missing any required field is malformed; the server MUST reject it with JSON-RPC error code -32602 (Invalid params). On HTTP, the response status MUST be 400 Bad Request.
claim_checks.note: Both values are MUST on the page.

claim_checks.claim: On HTTP there is nothing to shut down: each request is its own POST ✅[13]
claim_checks.page_says: Each request is its own POST; … (terminated with HTTP DELETE) … None of these mechanisms are part of this revision.
claim_checks.note: The page removes the legacy session and its DELETE termination, and tells a modern-only server to answer DELETE with 405, so no shutdown step remains.

claim_checks.claim: `notifications/tools/list_changed`, delivered on a GET stream or the open connection ✅[4][13]
claim_checks.page_says: listChanged: Support for list change notifications (for prompts, resources, and tools) … The server MAY send JSON-RPC requests and notifications on the stream.
claim_checks.note: Legacy (2025-11-25) column. The cited legacy pages [4] (lifecycle, transports) never name `notifications/tools/list_changed`; searched 'list_changed'. The name appears in [13], but that is a 2026-07-28 page and ties it to subscriptions/listen, not a GET stream, so it cannot support a legacy claim. The name does appear in the 2025-11-25 security page ([4a-sess]), which this cell does not cite. Name gap, so CRITICAL_FAIL.

claim_checks.claim: A missing resource is error `-32602` in 2026-07-28 (it was `-32002` before; clients should still accept `-32002`) ✅[17][3]
claim_checks.page_says: If the requested resource does not exist, servers MUST return a JSON-RPC error with code -32602 (Invalid Params). … clients SHOULD also accept -32002 as a resource not found error
claim_checks.note: The changelog [3] also records the change from -32002 to -32602.

claim_checks.claim: The client gathers the input and retries the original request with a new `id`, `inputResponses` and the echoed `requestState` ✅[23]
claim_checks.page_says: The JSON-RPC id MUST be different between the initial request and the retry … the client MUST echo back the exact value of that field when retrying the original request
claim_checks.note: The page's workflow also says the client gathers the requested information, then retries the original request including it.

claim_checks.claim: Worked example (2026-07-28, from the spec): `tools/call` id 2 returns an `input_required` result asking for a GitHub username via form elicitation; the client retries `tools/call` as id 3 with `inputResponses: {"github_login":{"action":"accept","content":{"name":"octocat"}}}` and the same `requestState` ✅[14][23]
claim_checks.page_says: "id": 2 … "resultType": "input_required" … "mode": "form", "message": "Please provide your GitHub username" … Retry with Input Responses: … "id": 3 … "name": "octocat"
claim_checks.note: The ids, the form mode, the github_login key, the accept action, the octocat value and the repeated requestState all match the tools page example.

claim_checks.claim: optional `MCP-Session-Id`; 400 without it; 404 when ended; client `DELETE` to end ✅[4]
claim_checks.page_says: Servers that require a session ID SHOULD respond to requests without an MCP-Session-Id header (other than initialization) with HTTP 400 Bad Request. … SHOULD send an HTTP DELETE
claim_checks.note: 2025-11-25 column. 404 after termination is MUST and matches. But the 400 rule is SHOULD, and it applies only to servers that require a session ID (initialization is excepted); the cell states it with no modal and no condition. The client DELETE is also SHOULD, and the server MAY answer 405. These are SHOULD rules written as plain statements, with dropped conditions, so WARN.

claim_checks.claim: keep old endpoints only for old clients, add Streamable HTTP ✅[13]
claim_checks.page_says: Servers wanting to support older clients should: … Continue to host both the SSE and POST endpoints of the old transport, alongside the new “MCP endpoint”
claim_checks.note: The page adds that existing HTTP+SSE implementations SHOULD migrate to Streamable HTTP. The decision-table advice matches both.

claim_checks.page_says: Receive notifications/tools/list_changed when tools change … allowing the server to communicate to the client, without the client first sending data via HTTP POST
claim_checks.note: [15] covers the 2026-07-28 option (toolsListChanged filter). [4] (2025-11-25 transports) covers the legacy GET SSE stream. Each era is checked against its own page.

claim_checks.claim: Alternative transports must follow established best practice for their protocol ✅[26]
claim_checks.page_says: Implementations using alternative transports MUST follow established security best practices for their protocol.
claim_checks.note: The modal matches (MUST), but the claim drops the qualifier 'security': the page requires security best practices, not best practice in general. Dropped qualifier, so WARN.

claim_checks.claim: Server must validate the token and that it was issued for this server as audience; invalid or expired gives `401`; insufficient scope gives `403` with `error="insufficient_scope"` and a `scope` listing what the operation needs ✅[26]
claim_checks.page_says: Invalid or expired tokens MUST receive an HTTP 401 response. … with insufficient scope during runtime operations, the server SHOULD respond with: … HTTP 403 Forbidden
claim_checks.note: Token validation, the audience check and the 401 are MUST and match. The 403 with insufficient_scope and a scope parameter is SHOULD on the page, but here it sits under the step's leading 'Server must', and the flow is introduced as 'steps are normative unless marked'. A SHOULD raised to MUST level, so CRITICAL_FAIL.

claim_checks.claim: Resources ✅[17]: servers must validate URIs and sanitize `file://` paths against traversal.
claim_checks.page_says: Servers MUST validate all resource URIs … Servers MUST sanitize file paths to prevent directory traversal attacks when serving file:// resources
claim_checks.note: The check mark labels the sentence after the colon; both requirements are MUST on the page.

claim_checks.claim: SSRF through metadata URLs (clients should require HTTPS and block private ranges, and use an egress proxy on servers) ✅[30]
claim_checks.page_says: SHOULD require HTTPS for all OAuth-related URLs in production environments … SHOULD block requests to private and reserved IP address ranges … SHOULD consider using an egress proxy
claim_checks.note: Two gaps. The HTTPS rule's condition 'in production environments' (and its scope, OAuth-related URLs) is dropped. 'SHOULD consider using an egress proxy' becomes 'should … use an egress proxy', a modal raised short of MUST level. The claim's own 'should' governs over the list's leading 'required mitigations', so WARN, not CRITICAL_FAIL.

conflicts.where_loser_is: ## 5. What the experiments showed that the spec text does not say

conflicts.topic: Whether 2026-07-28 removed any feature. The sources agree: [21] says none was removed 'under this policy', and [3] lists removals (ping, logging/setLevel, the initialize handshake). The doc's paraphrase of [21] drops the qualifier and so contradicts [3] and the doc's own section 2.2
conflicts.winner: [3] rank 1 (consistent with [21] rank 1 read in full)
conflicts.loser: doc paraphrase of [21]: 'No feature has been removed yet'

violations.evidence: S4: the legacy cell names `notifications/tools/list_changed`, but the cited legacy pages [4] do not name it, and [13] is a 2026-07-28 page (versions stay apart).
S12: step 9 puts the 403 insufficient_scope response under 'Server must'; [26] says the server SHOULD respond with 403.

S8: the 2025-11-25 Sessions cell states '400 without it' and 'client DELETE to end' as plain facts; [4] has SHOULD for both, limits the 400 to servers that require a session ID, and lets the server answer DELETE with 405.
S11: drops 'security' from [26]'s 'MUST follow established security best practices for their protocol'.
S14: drops 'in production environments' from the HTTPS rule and turns 'SHOULD consider using an egress proxy' into 'should … use an egress proxy' ([30]).

Found in the conflict audit, outside the claims.json sample (not counted in coverage or factual_grounding): section 3.2 says 'No feature has been removed yet ✅[21]'. [21] says 'No features have been removed under this policy yet.' [3] says 'Remove ping, logging/setLevel, and notifications/roots/list_changed.' The dropped qualifier makes 3.2 contradict [3] and section 2.2. This is a misparaphrase, not a disagreement between sources, so it is graded as a dropped qualifier (WARN), not as a KB-17 CRITICAL_FAIL.

The doc is organized by research question (Q1 to Q4), not by role. Role 1 has no section of its own: the mental model and analogy sit in the Summary. Role 2 has no section of its own: it is spread over 1.1 Roles and the 2.1 'Controlled by' table. The role-5 section ## 2 also carries mechanism (the MRTR and subscriptions flows).
The section points to a temporary scratchpad path and says the files 'were not kept'. Nothing can be reproduced, and claims cited only to [E1]-[E6] cannot be re-checked.
